comments.body:
## 2026-11-03: implemented; Gerrit 3279 pushed

Root cause: commit `3bde5613718` changed `_opcert_trust_root` (`src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py`) to fall back own key -> pinned key -> the public key embedded in the SSHSIG envelope (`envelope_key`), returning no key (`foreign_key`) only under `verify.require_environment`. The messages in `env_identity.py` and 3 passages of `docs/concurrency.md` were not updated with it.

Scope found by a string grep, beyond the 2 messages: the module and `reidentification_warning` docstrings, `docs/concurrency.md` lines 1044/1056/1077, and the `.opcert-key` carry-over entry plus its docs table row ("without it no existing attestation verifies, even with the matching .env-id"). Once the warning was reworded, that entry contradicted the sentence above it in the same rendered message. It now states the measured hazard: under the old id, the first op-cert signed mints a new key (`_opcert_signing.py:362`), after which certs from the old key fail as `mismatch` unless that key is pinned (`test_cert_under_an_unpinned_previous_key_still_fails`).

Tests: `test_reidentification_warning_says_old_attestations_still_certify` and `test_divergence_report_says_old_attestations_still_certify` failed on origin/main (missing `verify.require_environment`; then the carry-over contradiction) and pass now. `test_env_identity_guard.py` + c21f + d909 suites: 53 passed. Old-phrase grep: 9 hits before, 0 after. `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0.

Commit `957db322151`-lineage on Gerrit change 3279 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/3279).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Two operator-facing messages in `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py` still say that a tracker re-clone makes the old environment's op-cert attestations unverifiable, with a `foreign_key` verdict at the claim and close gates, and that they "must be re-earned":

- the `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` fsck line returned by `divergence_report` (`env_identity.py:268-277`);
- the mint warning returned by `reidentification_warning` (`env_identity.py:163-177`).

Since commit `3bde5613718` (bug `c21f-6f29-5d2d-4a5a`, "Stop gating op-certs on signing environment") that is false by default. `_opcert_trust_root` (`src/rebar/_opcert_verify.py:113-140`) falls back from the own key to a pinned key to the public key embedded in the SSHSIG envelope (`trust_basis: envelope_key`), so a cert signed under a lost identity still certifies. It returns no key, and the cert turns `foreign_key`, only when `verify.require_environment` is set (`_opcert_verify.py:134-135` and `:239-249`). That is pinned by `test_cross_environment_cert_certifies_when_enforcement_unset` and `test_enforcement_on_withholds_the_envelope_key_fallback` in `tests/unit/test_opcert_cross_environment_c21f.py`. `docs/manifest-signing.md:42`, `docs/reuse-surface.md:137` and `src/rebar/schemas/verify_signature_result.schema.json` already describe `foreign_key` that way.

An operator who reads the messages re-runs plan-review and completion gates that do not need it.

A string grep for the old claim found it in 3 more places that the original description missed:

- the `env_identity.py` module docstring (lines 3-7: "attestations from another environment do not verify here ... store-wide `foreign_key` verdict") and the `reidentification_warning` docstring (line 154: "has just orphaned its own attestations");
- `docs/concurrency.md` §"Re-cloning the tracker" (lines 1030-1089), which contradicts its own closing paragraph (line 1081, "A re-clone no longer invalidates op-cert attestations"): line 1044 ("losing it fails **silently and late**"), lines 1056-1060 ("has just orphaned that environment's attestations"), and lines 1076-1077 ("discovering the loss one ticket at a time at a gate").

## Approach

Reword each site to the behaviour `_opcert_trust_root` implements, using the closing paragraph of `docs/concurrency.md` (line 1081) as the reference text, because it is already correct and is the canonical operator doc. Message wording:

- Mint warning, re-clone branch: the old identity's attestations still certify here on the public key embedded in each signature; they turn `foreign_key` only under the opt-in `verify.require_environment`, which trusts only that environment's own or pinned keys. A re-clone costs one continuous audit identity and the ability to sign as the old identity. The `REBAR_ALLOW_ENV_REIDENTIFY` line stays unchanged.
- Mint warning, `.opcert-key` carry-over entry (`CARRY_OVER`, `env_identity.py:56-60`): it now says "without it no existing attestation verifies, even with the matching .env-id", which contradicts the corrected sentence above it in the same rendered warning. Reword it to the measured behaviour: under the old id, the first op-cert this clone signs mints a new key (`ensure_opcert_key(..., create_if_missing=True)`, `src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:362`), and attestations the old key signed then fail as `mismatch` unless that key is pinned (`test_cert_under_an_unpinned_previous_key_still_fails`, `tests/unit/test_opcert_own_principal_rotation_d909.py:174`).
- `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` line: the same two facts replace "cannot be verified here ... must be re-earned". The overlap wording from Gerrit 3270 (`7ea86184dac`) and the carry-over names stay unchanged.

In `docs/concurrency.md`, the re-clone bullet keeps its recovery advice and says to restore `.env-id` together with `.opcert-key`. With the old id but a newly minted key, a cert signed under the old key is checked against the new key and fails as `mismatch` unless that key is pinned (`test_cert_under_an_unpinned_previous_key_still_fails`, `tests/unit/test_opcert_own_principal_rotation_d909.py:174`).

No verifier behaviour changes; this is text only.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py`: 2 message strings, the `.opcert-key` `CARRY_OVER` entry, and 2 docstrings.
- `docs/concurrency.md`: the prose of §"Re-cloning the tracker" (lines 1030-1089). Edit the paragraph at lines 1044-1048, the re-clone bullet at lines 1056-1060, and the sentence at lines 1076-1077. In the carry-over table, reword the `.opcert-key` row's "nothing verifies, even with the matching `.env-id`" to the same `mismatch` behaviour. The closing paragraph at line 1081 stays as it is.
- `tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py`: new assertions on both messages.

## Testing

- New tests in `tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py`, written first and failing on `origin/main`:
  - `test_reidentification_warning_says_old_attestations_still_certify`: the unacknowledged warning names `verify.require_environment` and `foreign_key`, and contains none of "unverifiable", "re-earned", "cannot be verified" or "no existing attestation".
  - `test_divergence_report_says_old_attestations_still_certify`: the `ENV_ID_MISMATCH` line built from overlapping spans makes the same assertions.
- Edge: the acknowledged `NOTE:` form is unchanged; the existing `test_override_acknowledges_and_quietens_the_warning` still passes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Neither message claims that attestations become unverifiable by default, and both name `verify.require_environment` as the condition for `foreign_key`; verified by the 2 new tests passing in `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py`, which fail on `origin/main`.
- [x] The existing tests still pass: `pytest tests/interfaces/store/test_env_identity_guard.py tests/unit/test_opcert_cross_environment_c21f.py tests/unit/test_opcert_own_principal_rotation_d909.py` exits 0.
- [x] No old-claim phrase remains: `git grep -nF -e 're-earned' -e 'unverifiable here' -e 'cannot be verified here' -e 'do not verify here' -e 'orphaned its own attestations' -e 'orphaned that' -e 'silently and late' -e 'one ticket at a time at a gate' -- src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py docs/concurrency.md` prints nothing. Worked example: on `origin/main` (`c6f116f1ae8`) the same command with `-c` prints `docs/concurrency.md:3` (lines 1044, 1056, 1077) and `src/rebar/_store/env_identity.py:6` (lines 5, 154, 170-171, 273-274); after the change both counts are absent.
- [x] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0 with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on `PATH`.

file_impact.reason: reword the mint warning (incl. the .opcert-key carry-over entry), the ENV_ID_MISMATCH line and 2 docstrings to the envelope_key / verify.require_environment policy
remove the stale lost-attestation claims from the re-clone section and its .opcert-key table row
assert the reworded text of both messages
